sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Anti-FLAG immunofluorescence confirmed surface expression of the FLAG-tagged full-length receptor (L4/L5). Structural studies (L1) produced a cryo-EM-quality complex, indicating the receptor traffics and folds correctly with the N-terminal tag.
sites.rationale: MLNR has no signal peptide in the canonical sequence; the N-terminus (residues 1–37) is extracellular per the topology landmarks. A prepend (insert_after_residue=0) places the tag immediately before M1 on the extracellular face, exactly as done in the PRESTO-TANGO constructs (L4/L5) and the structural study (L1). The position is topology-derived because neither paper names a specific residue number for the junction — the tag is at the sole extracellular terminus. The 37-residue extracellular N-terminal domain provides ample space for a short epitope tag upstream of TM1 (boundary at residue 38). PRESTO-TANGO platform (PMC4424118): full-length MLNR/GPR38 engineered with a cleavable signal sequence followed by a FLAG epitope tag at the 5′-end; the signal sequence is cleaved post-translationally, leaving FLAG at the extracellular N-terminus of the membrane-anchored receptor. Anti-FLAG immunofluorescence confirmed both total and surface expression. Additionally, PMC10017046 reports a structural construct with N-terminal BRIL+FLAG+10×His prepended to full-length MTLR for cryo-EM.

sources.claim: At the 5′-end, we included a cleavable signal sequence to promote membrane localization 23 and a FLAG epitope tag in order to be able to monitor cell surface expression by immunohistochemistry.

literature_notes: L2 (C-terminal LgBiT) and L3 (C-terminal EGFP on truncated constructs at Δ385, Δ375, Δ369) all map to the intracellular C-terminus (topology: 359–412 intracellular) and are recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports an insertion in any extracellular loop (ECL1 97–112, ECL2 178–246, ECL3 321–337) with a named residue or loop-level precedent, so no internal sites are proposed. L4 and L5 both ground the same N-terminal FLAG site; L4 is cited as the primary clip because it describes the construct design, and L5 confirms surface display.

literature_other_positions.note: LgBiT inserted at the C-terminus of full-length MTLR (residue 412, intracellular C-tail 359–412) as part of the NanoBiT strategy for structural studies; not an extracellular surface site.
